sources.locator: "Armistice of 22 June 1940", revision 1370957537, § lead and § Battle of France

explanation: The article gives the armistice as the outcome of a campaign of the war: **"following the decisive German victory in the Battle of France, the armistice established a German occupation zone in Northern and Western France that encompassed about three-fifths of France's European territory, including all English Channel and Atlantic Ocean ports."** § Battle of France is the account of how it came to be signed: the best French armies lost in the northern encirclement, the government relocated to Bordeaux on 10 June, Paris was declared an open city, and Reynaud resigned on 16 June in a cabinet full of pro-armistice ministers, Pétain becoming prime minister.
